builder_claims.claim: Template 490267 renders 3 stages / 76 days with real sub-processes
builder_claims.evidence: shots/sb-template-1440.png vs shots/live-template-1440.png. Sandbox: STAGES 3, TOTAL TIME 76 days, Stage1 Yarn Processing 20d (Yarn Processing 15d, Processed Yarn QC 5d+approval), Stage2 Yarn Weaving 50d (Fabric Initial Sample 20d+approval, Complete Production 30d), Stage3 Fabric Finishing 6d (Washing 3d, QC Fabric 3d+approval). 20+50+6=76 arithmetic consistent. Stage AND sub-process names match live's flowchart exactly.
builder_claims.fix: None. Note live's template view shows no durations at all (ManageProcessDetailsComponent never renders estimatedDays) — the day totals are enrichment, not parity, and are internally consistent.

builder_claims.claim: Workflow 133044983: Yarn Processing done, Yarn Weaving in progress, reads 38%; only To do/In progress/Done, zero HALTED
builder_claims.evidence: probe.json + shots/probe-pipeline.png. Reads '38% - 1/4 stages done - 1 in progress - 3/8 tasks'. 4 stages (Yarn Processing, Yarn Weaving, Fabric Finishing, Fabric Dyeing) x 2 tasks = 8; done = Yarn Processing, Processed Yarn QC, Fabric Initial Sample = 3; 3/8 = 37.5% -> 38%. Arithmetic reproduces. Columns are exactly TO DO / IN PROGRESS / DONE. Jobs-list Halted filter returns 'Showing 0 order jobs', corroborating the zero-HALTED data claim.
builder_claims.fix: None on the data. See M-11: HALTED still EXISTS in live's model (WorkflowStatus + WorkflowStepStatus enums, grey #d1d5db legend swatch), so 'zero HALTED' is true of today's rows, not of the model.

Cards: 'Yarn Processing' x=1104 (DONE), 'Processed Yarn QC' x=1104 (DONE), 'Fabric Initial Sample' x=1104 (DONE), 'Complete Production' x=796 (IN PROGRESS), Washing/Base Fabric QC/Sampling Completion/QC Fabric x=485 (TO DO). builder_claims.fix: None. The original complaint is genuinely fixed, and workflow-ops.ts documents the stage-dominance rule as display-only without rewriting the row.

findings.title: Right half of the production table is unreachable at every desktop width; row actions cannot be clicked
findings.live_does: Live renders the item list as full-width card markup inside a 63% column with no clipping; every per-item control (edit, start, view-workflow, checkbox) is directly clickable (custom-ordered-item-list.component.html:20-62).
findings.we_do: The table sits in a div.overflow-x-auto measuring scrollWidth 1112 / clientWidth 758 — 354px permanently hidden. Measured identical at 1440 AND 1600 (sb-diag.json order@1440, order@1600): the extra 160px of viewport becomes page whitespace, not table width. ARTISAN is cut mid-word ('Fabr...'), WORKFLOW % is cut, and the entire STAGES column plus all three row actions (Open job / edit / delete) are off-screen. There is no visible scrollbar or affordance.
findings.evidence: shots/sb-order-1440-s1.png, shots/sb-order-1600-s1.png (clip at identical x=1022 with ~380px empty to the right), shots/probe-order-scrolled-right.png (content is correct once force-scrolled), .harness/audit-2026-08-16/sb-diag.json
findings.fix: Let the Production card span the full content width instead of sharing a row with the 390px Pricing rail — move Pricing/Payment/Customer below the table, or make the grid 1-col under ~1700px. Then drop the fixed min-widths so the 9 columns fit in ~1150px. If a scroller must remain, add a persistent scrollbar and a sticky right-hand actions column so Open job/edit/delete are never scrolled away.

findings.title: Mobile (390px) is unusable — the sidebar never collapses; this is a regression against live
findings.live_does: Live collapses its sidebar to a ~62px icon rail at 390px and stacks content in a single readable column (shots/live-order-390-s0.png).
findings.we_do: The 240px sidebar stays fully expanded at 390px, leaving ~150px for content. The DRAFT banner renders one word per line, 'Custom Order #132440539' overflows, Cancel order/Delete are cut off, the jobs stat cards are clipped mid-number ('1,3', '1,1', '21'), and a div.flex (403px) overflows a 255px parent with no scroll affordance.
findings.evidence: shots/sb-order-390-s0.png, shots/sb-jobs-390-s0.png vs shots/live-order-390-s0.png; sb-diag.json order@390 hoff entry 'DIV 403/255 flex items-center gap-3'
findings.fix: Auto-collapse the app shell sidebar to an icon rail (or an off-canvas drawer) below ~1024px — the collapse toggle already exists, it simply is not driven by a breakpoint. Then re-test all four screens at 390.

findings.title: Impact Dashboard is entirely missing
findings.live_does: custom-order-detail.component.html renders <wv-order-impact-dashboard [custom]=true> full-width below both columns: an eyebrow 'Impact Dashboard' + h2 'Custom order impact', 8 metric cards (Fabric meters/CO2 offset/Water saved/Artisan hours/Women artisan hours/Stitching hours/Women stitching hours/Total work hours), a 15-column 'Order item impact' table (Workflow, Order Item, Type, Status, Pending Reason, Fabric, CO2, Water, Artisan, Women Artisan, Stitching, Women Stitching, Total, Version, Updated), a 'Skipped workflows' list, and a 'Recalculate impact' button (POST /trigger/impact/custom-order/{id}).
findings.we_do: Nothing. The page ends at the production table; only headings are Custom Order / Production / Pricing.
findings.evidence: shots/probe-live-order-bottom.png (live table populated: FABRIC/COMPLETE, 50 m, 13.6 kg, 300 L, 800 hrs, 520 hrs; PARTIAL rows carry pending reason 'avg artisan work hours per meter not configured'), shots/sb-order-1440-s3.png (sandbox page ends), probe.json h2h3
findings.fix: Port the impact dashboard as a full-width section below the production table. Note live's impact table is where order items #132448589 and #132450307 actually surface — porting it also closes the C6 traceability caveat.

findings.title: Per-item workflow NOTE is dropped — an operator loses dispatch commitments
findings.live_does: Each item with processAssociated.note renders an amber badge (border-amber-300 bg-amber-50 text-amber-900, sticky_note_2 icon) — on this very order: 'Note: Aug 13 : Mariam will dispatch the Kantha fabric within 4-5 days' on KMD3000026 (custom-ordered-item-list.component.html:115-125).
findings.we_do: No note anywhere. probe.json: hasNoteMariam=false, noteMentions=0 across the whole rendered page.
findings.fix: Render workflow.note as an amber badge under the item row in the production table (or in the expanded history disclosure). This is free-text ops commentary that exists nowhere else.

findings.title: GLOBAL NOTE card missing
findings.live_does: Always-present 'Global Note' card with a textarea and a Save button gated on dirty-state (POST /update/custom-order/global-note). Currently holds 'July 27: 3 kantha stitch fabric is in production stage. Jallaluddin will share the images of initial...'.
findings.evidence: shots/live-order-390-s0.png, probe3.json liveImpactSnippet ('sticky_note_2 GLOBAL NOTE SAVE'), probe.json h2h3

findings.title: Artisan Payments has no sandbox screen at all
findings.live_does: /manage-workflow/artisan-payments — 3 clickable stat tiles (Pending/Approved/Paid totals + counts), 3 filters (status/workflow/artisan), an 11-column records table with INLINE-EDITABLE rate on PENDING rows, Approve + delete row actions, an approval dialog with notes, and a Settings tab editing artisan-incentive-config key/value pairs. 9 dedicated endpoints. Plus the base-pay consistency guard (util/base-pay-consistency.ts) that exists specifically to prevent the 'shows base pay but is never paid' state.
findings.we_do: No route, no screen, no link.
findings.evidence: live hub tiles enumerated from manage-process/model/process-dashboard-items.ts:60-68 (6 tiles: Manage Template, Manage Process, Manage Custom Process, Artisan Payments, Manage Feedback, Manage Custom Feedback)
findings.fix: Scope Artisan Payments as its own screen. Until then say so on the instance page — live shows a green 'Artisan payment is ready for review' banner with a View Payment Ledger button on every COMPLETED workflow, and we show nothing.

findings.title: Base Pay / m is not displayed — the money field that drives payment calculation
findings.live_does: Each artisan row carries a 'Base Pay / m' (fabric) or 'Base Pay / unit' input bound to assignment.basePay, alongside Metres. Visible on both 133044983 and 114027735.
findings.we_do: Rows show only name + quantity + level ('50 METER', 'Job level' / 'Task: Fabric Initial Sample'). No base pay at any level.
findings.evidence: shots/live-instance-1440.png and shots/live-instance2-1440-s0.png (Base Pay / m 0.00) vs shots/sb-instance-1440.png, probe3.json sbArtisanCard
findings.fix: Show basePay per artisan row read-only. Also surface the cross-level conflict the live guard checks for — an artisan carrying two different rates is silently never paid.

findings.title: Two contradictory end dates on the same screen, unexplained
findings.we_do: Header shows PLANNED 12 Sept 2026 and PROJECTED 12 Sept 2026, while the SCHEDULE card directly below shows 'Ends -> 29 Aug 2026' with its last stage (Fabric Dyeing) ending 29 Aug 2026. Two dates 14 days apart, no label explaining the difference.
findings.fix: Either reconcile the schedule roll-up with PLANNED, or label the schedule card explicitly as a what-if simulator ('projection if you move/extend stages') so the 29 Aug is not read as the job's end date.

findings.title: Sub-process capture properties are dropped, and datatype/valuetype is lost
findings.live_does: Properties hang off the individual node and render as '• {{key}}: {{datatype}}, {{valuetype}}'. On this template live shows 'Comments on the Quality: string, deferred' on the QC Fabric sub-process (Stage 3).
findings.we_do: 'DETAILS TO CAPTURE' chips are attached to the STAGE and show the key only. Stage 3 (Fabric Finishing) shows NO details-to-capture block at all, so 'Comments on the Quality' is not rendered anywhere; Stage 1 shows 'Target GSM', Stage 2 'Original Sample EPI * PPI'.
findings.evidence: shots/live-template-1440.png (tooltip visible on QC Fabric) vs shots/sb-template-1440.png and sb-report.json template text
findings.fix: Attach capture fields to the task they belong to, not the stage, and include sub-process properties. Render the datatype and valuetype — 'deferred' is what tells an operator the field must be filled before the task can complete.

findings.title: Delete button does not respond to a click
findings.live_does: Live's template VIEW page has no Delete at all (delete lives on the template list row, behind a ConfirmDialog).
findings.we_do: A 'Delete' button is rendered in the header. Playwright resolved the locator, scrolled it into view, and the click timed out after 30s — the element is not actionable (disabled, pointer-events blocked, or covered).
findings.fix: Either wire it (with a confirm dialog and a visible refusal if the sandbox blocks the write) or remove it. A rendered button that cannot be clicked is exactly the dead control the brief asks about. NOT fully diagnosed — needs a follow-up pass to determine whether it is disabled or obscured by the Feedback widget.

findings.title: Live order-level controls absent (read-only by design, but the gap should be explicit)
findings.live_does: Link with Zoho; Edit Order; Cancel Order; Send Confirmation E-mail; PARTIAL READY and PARTIAL FULFILLMENT dialogs (with the dispatch-cannot-exceed-ready guard); ADJUST PRICING; + Add Items; per-item edit/delete/start-workflow icons; per-item and select-all shipping checkboxes.
findings.we_do: Cancel order, Delete, Add item, Adjust pricing, and (clipped) per-row Open job/edit/delete. No Zoho link, no Edit order, no confirmation e-mail, no partial ready/fulfilment capture, no checkboxes.
findings.evidence: probe3.json liveImpactSnippet ('LINK WITH ZOHOEDIT ORDERCANCEL ORDER ... SEND CONFIRMATION E-MAIL PARTIAL FULFILLMENT PARTIAL READY') vs shots/sb-order-1440-s0.png
findings.fix: Acceptable for a read-only preview, but the DRAFT banner should name what is intentionally absent so a reviewer does not read the screen as feature-complete.

findings.title: Ready/dispatch records are not identified by order item
findings.live_does: Every ready and shipment chip prints 'Custom Order Item #{{customOrderItemId}}' alongside the product name and SKU.
findings.we_do: Chips print the ready/dispatch record id (#166662493, #152709488) and no item id.
findings.evidence: probe3.json liveImpactSnippet ('Custom Order Item #132440552') vs probe2.json expanded
findings.fix: Add the customOrderItemId to each chip.

findings.title: Planned end date off by one day vs live
findings.fix: Likely an epoch->date timezone boundary. Format in the same zone live uses (dd-MM-yyyy off the raw epoch).

findings.title: Dispatch chip renders 'pkg PACKAGE'
findings.we_do: Literal text 'pkg PACKAGE' — reads like a placeholder leaked into the UI.
findings.fix: Confirm whether 'PACKAGE' is the real stored value; if it is a sentinel, hide the chip instead of printing it.

findings.title: HALTED would render in the In progress column rather than its own state
findings.live_does: HALTED is a first-class value in BOTH WorkflowStatus and WorkflowStepStatus, with its own legend swatch and grey fill #d1d5db.
findings.we_do: Three columns only; columnForStatus() routes HALTED (and any unknown status) to 'doing'. The card still prints its true label, so it does not lie — and today zero rows are HALTED.
findings.fix: No action needed now; this is documented and honest. Revisit if a Loom resync reintroduces HALTED rows.

findings.title: Live's flowchart shape is not reproduced
findings.live_does: A left-to-right flow canvas: 240x100 step boxes (#F1F5F9) joined by arrows, with rotated-45 diamonds (#8B8EC7) hanging below each step.
findings.we_do: A vertical list of stage cards with task rows.
findings.fix: Deliberate redesign and arguably more legible; flagged only so the divergence is a decision on record, not an oversight.

not_verified: Write persistence: 'Mark done' on the pipeline and the steps-write behaviour for STANDARD-order jobs were NOT driven — clicking them mutates application data, which is outside this audit's read-only remit. The instance page does render explicit sandbox write-refusal notices for the artisan and schedule cards ('sandbox-only write: refusing to edit a live-synced custom workflow'), so those two surfaces are honest. The pipeline's 'Mark done' carries only a 'Sandbox test DB only' label — recommend a follow-up pass on a disposable record.
Instance delete and discussion 501s were not exercised (write paths).
